newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler denies plans for Rover car alliance.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler denies plans for Rover car alliance.

text.p: Chrysler Corp Friday denied a British newspaper report that it is planning to jointly develop new car models with Bayerische Motoren Werke AG's Rover Group to be produced in Britain.

Chrysler spokesman Michael Aberlich said there was no truth to the report in London's Sunday Times newspaper, which said that if a deal is reached in the next few months, the new car may replace the Rover 400 model and larger versions of the Rover 200.
"We haven't been discussing that particular product," Aberlich said, adding that he is unaware of any vehicle cooperation between the two automakers.

Chrysler and BMW last year announced a joint venture to produce a new range of four-cylinder engines in Brazil for use in Chrysler and Rover cars. Chrysler said it will use the engines in export versions of the Neon small car and other new models to be developed solely by Chrysler.
